group:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-famous.overview: 文章分析电动车更容易让人晕车的原因：单踏板驾驶使减速过急，车内屏幕过多让乘客不看窗外；又指出自动驾驶汽车可能带来新挑战，车企正用更好的技术应对。
group:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-famous.fullTranslationZh:
比起燃油车，你坐电动车时晕车更厉害吗？不只你一个人这样——而说到自动驾驶汽车，情况可能更糟。
尽管科学家还不完全确定晕车的成因，但它与乘客失去预判车辆接下来如何移动的能力有关。你在车里看杂志时，眼睛会向大脑发出车子静止不动的信号。然而，大脑却能察觉到车子的振动和转弯。这会让大脑感到混乱，使你开始觉得难受。
就电动车而言，据美国能源部称，单踏板驾驶常被认为是让人晕车的原因。这一个踏板同时负责加速和刹车——司机踩下踏板来提速，松开踏板来减速。如果停止加速，单踏板系统就会自动让车减速并停下。因此，这种系统造成的减速比燃油车更急，这可能会引起晕车。
另一项可能也与晕车有关的技术进步，是电动车内越来越大、数量也越来越多的屏幕。据《对话》网站报道，这些屏幕用过多的视觉信息让使用者应接不暇，使他们不愿往车外看。乘客因此接收不到“正确”的视觉信号，比如移动的周围景物，这就可能引发晕车。
遗憾的是，即便人们适应了电动车的行驶方式、晕车有所减轻，自动驾驶汽车可能又会给他们带来新的挑战。一项研究显示，多达 12% 的美国人在乘坐自动驾驶汽车时可能会晕车。
为了确保新型汽车得到广泛使用，汽车制造商正努力用更好的技术解决这类问题。例如，据《汽车杂志》报道，日本本田公司正通过改进发动机来减轻汽车“猛烈”的加速。

selectedLongSentences.analysisZh: 主句是 it has to do with …（它与……有关），it 指晕车。Although 引导让步状语从句，从句里 what causes motion sickness 是 sure 后的宾语从句。with 后面是动名词复合结构 passengers being deprived of …：passengers 是 being deprived 的逻辑主语，be deprived of 表示“被夺去、失去”，宾语是 the ability to predict future movements（预判接下来动作的能力）。第 28 题考的就是这个短语。

selectedLongSentences.analysisZh: 主干是 These screens overburden users with visual information（这些屏幕用视觉信息让使用者负担过重）。which 引导非限制性定语从句，指代前面整件事；discourage sb from doing 表示“使某人不愿做某事”，所以是信息过多让人不往外看。according to The Conversation 交代消息来源。第 29 题的答案就落在 which 从句上。

discourseStructure.summary: 先以电动车让人更晕车的问题开篇，再讲晕车的一般机理，接着分析电动车的两个具体原因，然后指出自动驾驶车的新挑战，最后说车企正在用技术解决。

paragraphs.summary: 问读者坐电动车是否更晕车，并说自动驾驶车可能更糟。
晕车与乘客无法预判车的动作有关：看杂志时眼睛以为车不动，大脑却感到振动和转弯。
单踏板驾驶一松脚就自动减速，减速比燃油车更急，可能引起晕车。
车内屏幕越来越多，视觉信息过量让乘客不看窗外，接收不到正确的视觉信号。
即便适应了电动车，自动驾驶车仍可能让多达 12% 的美国人晕车。
车企正用更好的技术解决问题，如本田改进发动机以减轻猛烈加速。

question:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-fam.questionFocus: 借后文读杂志晕车的例子，推断短语 being deprived of 在句中的意思。
question:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-fam.stemTranslationZh: 第 2 段中短语 “being deprived of” 的意思可能是什么？

evidence.quote: Although scientists aren’t exactly sure what causes motion sickness, it has to do with passengers being deprived of the ability to predict future movements.
When you read a magazine in a car, your eyes will signal to your brain that the car is still.
However, your brain will recognize the vibrations(振动) and turns that the car makes.

trap.explanation: 放进去就成了“乘客只局限于预判车辆动作的能力”，像是还剩这种能力；例子里乘客恰恰预判不了。
放进去就成了“乘客满怀预判车辆动作的能力”，与眼睛以为车静止、乘客预判不了正相反。
放进去就成了“晕车与乘客正在培养预判能力有关”，可例子讲的是预判不了才晕车。

locationParaphrases.targetText: Although scientists aren’t exactly sure what causes motion sickness, it has to do with passengers being deprived of the ability to predict future movements.
locationParaphrases.answerText: your eyes will signal to your brain that the car is still
locationParaphrases.bridgeZh: 读杂志的例子说明乘客没法预判车怎么动
locationParaphrases.note: 题干短语 being deprived of 原词出现在原文。

locationParaphrases.targetText: Although scientists aren’t exactly sure what causes motion sickness, it has to do with passengers being deprived of the ability to predict future movements.
locationParaphrases.note: 短语后面跟着 the ability to predict（预判的能力），而例子说明乘客恰恰预判不了车的动作，所以这个短语必须表示“没有了这种能力”。放回去：晕车与乘客失去预判车辆下一步动作的能力有关，选 A。

question:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-fam.questionFocus: 把各选项放回单踏板和车内屏幕两处原因里核对，找出原文给出的晕车原因。
question:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-fam.stemTranslationZh: 什么可能导致人们在电动车里晕车更严重？
question:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-fam.locateFindZh: 按选项回单踏板和车内屏幕两处，核对原因

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 单踏板系统没法让车足够快地停下。

trap.sourceQuote: The deceleration caused by this system is thus more rapid than that of petrol cars, which may lead to motion sickness.
trap.optionText: The one-pedal system couldn’t stop the car fast enough.
trap.optionHighlight: couldn’t stop the car fast enough
trap.explanation: 原文说单踏板减速比燃油车更急（more rapid），减得太快才晕车；选项说成停得不够快，方向反了。

trapEvidence.quote: The deceleration caused by this system is thus more rapid than that of petrol cars, which may lead to motion sickness.

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 车内屏幕不提供吸引人的画面。

trap.claim: The screens inside do not provide appealing images.
trap.explanation: 原文说屏幕的问题是视觉信息太多（overburden users with visual information），让人顾不上看窗外，没说画面不吸引人。

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 乘客被分散了注意力，不去看车外的景色。

evidence.quote: These screens overburden users with visual information, which discourages them from looking outside, according to The Conversation.
Passengers thereby fail to take in the “correct” visual signals, such as the moving surroundings, which can trigger sickness.

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 人们适应创新设计需要时间。

trap.sourceQuote: Unfortunately, even when people adjust to the movements of electric cars and experience less car sickness, self-driving vehicles might be another challenge for them.
trap.sourceHighlight: adjust to the movements of electric cars and experience less car sickness
trap.optionText: It takes time for people to get adapted to creative designs.
trap.explanation: [[block:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-famous-schools-joint:reading-c:5]] 说人们适应（adjust to）电动车后晕车会减轻，适应是让晕车减轻的事，原文没把“适应要花时间”列为晕车原因。

trapEvidence.quote: Unfortunately, even when people adjust to the movements of electric cars and experience less car sickness, self-driving vehicles might be another challenge for them.

locationParaphrases.sourceText: Passengers are distracted from looking at outside views
locationParaphrases.targetText: These screens overburden users with visual information, which discourages them from looking outside, according to The Conversation.
locationParaphrases.note: 选项的“分心不看窗外”对应原文“屏幕信息太多，使人不愿往外看”（discourages them from looking outside）；接着原文说乘客因此看不到移动的外景（the moving surroundings），从而引发晕车。选 C。

question:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-fam.questionFocus: 根据车企正在采取的措施，推断晕车问题的前景，并把握结论的分寸。
question:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-fam.stemTranslationZh: 读者能从文中预测出什么？
question:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-fam.locateFindZh: 预测看结尾：读 [[block:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-famous-schools-joint:reading-c:6]] 车企正在做什么，再推晕车问题今后会怎样

trap.sourceQuote: To ensure the widespread usage of new types of vehicles, car producers are working to solve such problems with better technology.
trap.sourceHighlight: To ensure the widespread usage of new types of vehicles
trap.optionText: New types of vehicles have no bright future.
trap.explanation: 车企努力解决晕车，正是为了让新型汽车广泛使用（widespread usage），原文对新车的前景是积极的。

trapEvidence.quote: To ensure the widespread usage of new types of vehicles, car producers are working to solve such problems with better technology.

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 晕车问题最终有可能被避免。

evidence.quote: To ensure the widespread usage of new types of vehicles, car producers are working to solve such problems with better technology.
For example, Japanese company Honda is working on reducing the car’s “violent” acceleration by making changes to the engine, said Car Magazine.

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 人们很快就会克服晕车。

trap.sourceQuote: To ensure the widespread usage of new types of vehicles, car producers are working to solve such problems with better technology.
trap.sourceHighlight: are working to solve such problems
trap.optionText: People will get over car sickness pretty soon.
trap.explanation: 车企还在努力（are working to），[[block:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-famous-schools-joint:reading-c:5]] 也说自动驾驶车可能带来新挑战，推不出“很快”就能克服。

trapEvidence.quote: To ensure the widespread usage of new types of vehicles, car producers are working to solve such problems with better technology.

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 车内的电子设备将被拆除。

trap.claim: Electronic devices inside cars will be removed.
trap.explanation: 原文只说屏幕过多可能引发晕车，车企的办法是改进技术，比如改发动机，没说要拆掉车内设备。

locationParaphrases.sourceText: Car sickness can possibly be avoided in time
locationParaphrases.targetText: To ensure the widespread usage of new types of vehicles, car producers are working to solve such problems with better technology.
locationParaphrases.note: 原文没说晕车已经解决，只说车企正在用更好的技术解决这类问题（are working to solve），比如本田在改进发动机、减轻“猛烈”的加速。由此推出：随着技术改进，晕车有可能逐渐避免。选项用 possibly 和 in time 说到“有可能、要些时间”，没有说过头，选 B。

question:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-fam.questionFocus: 从开篇的问题和各段内容判断作者写这篇文章的目的。

trap.claim: To recommend ways to avoid car sickness.
trap.explanation: 全文没有教读者怎样防晕车；只有 [[block:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-famous-schools-joint:reading-c:6]] 提到车企在改进技术，那是厂家的做法，不是给读者的建议。

trap.sourceQuote: Unfortunately, even when people adjust to the movements of electric cars and experience less car sickness, self-driving vehicles might be another challenge for them.
trap.sourceHighlight: self-driving vehicles might be another challenge
trap.optionText: To promote the sales of self-driving cars.
trap.optionHighlight: promote the sales of self-driving cars
trap.explanation: 提到自动驾驶车时，原文说它可能是新的挑战（another challenge），还说多达 12% 的人可能晕车，并不是在推销。

trapEvidence.quote: Unfortunately, even when people adjust to the movements of electric cars and experience less car sickness, self-driving vehicles might be another challenge for them.

trap.claim: To clear misunderstandings of electric cars.
trap.explanation: 原文没说人们误解了电动车，[[block:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-famous-schools-joint:reading-c:1|You’re not alone]] 反而承认坐电动车确实可能更晕。

evidence.quote: Do you experience worse car sickness in electric cars than in petrol cars?
As for electric cars, one-pedal driving is often blamed for feelings of car sickness, according to the U. S. Department of Energy.
Another technological advance that can also be related to car sickness is the larger and increasing number of screens inside electric vehicles.

locationParaphrases.sourceText: To analyze possible causes of car sickness
locationParaphrases.targetText: Do you experience worse car sickness in electric cars than in petrol cars?
locationParaphrases.note: 全文围绕 [[block:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-famous-schools-joint:reading-c:1]] 抛出的问题展开：电动车为什么更容易让人晕车。先讲晕车的一般机理，再分别讲单踏板减速太急和车内屏幕太多，又说自动驾驶车可能更糟，用的多是 may、can 这类留余地的词。选项的“分析晕车的可能原因”正好概括这些内容，选 D。
